findings:
🟠 [oracle-integrity] MUST-FIX The depth-0-owned acceptance oracle `packages/relay/tests/adversarial/groups.test.ts` was modified, and pre-existing `fanout.test.ts` and `claims/store.test.ts` were also changed despite the specification allowing only `serve.reload.test.ts` and `claims.test.ts`; this bypasses the frozen harness and invalidates the supplied acceptance evidence. Restore every disallowed test change and make the implementation pass the original oracle.
🟠 [send-check-order] MUST-FIX `dispatch_needs_instance` was moved after subject ACL evaluation, violating the required address-rules-before-subject-ACL order and exposing subject-ownership results for malformed dispatches. Move this refusal into the address-rules block before all subject ACL queries.
🟠 [thread-timing-leak] MUST-FIX `resolveThreadContinuation` performs an unscoped route lookup and authorization/grant queries before comparing `route.group_id`, so an existing cross-group route follows a measurably different database path from a nonexistent route despite identical response bodies. Resolve the route with a group-scoped SQL predicate first, then perform thread authorization only on that scoped result.
